title: Map interval packing to circulation with gap capacities
problem: Solve the R03 weighted interval-packing dual exactly as a circulation for fixed-order robust berth buffers.
failure: If gap arcs point forward instead of backward, the three-vessel R03 witness has no profitable circulation and returns 0 instead of 3. Treating the flow objective alone as a buffer schedule also omits primal recovery.
correction: Place each positive-demand interval as a forward arc j->i with profit w_(j,i), and each gap k as a backward arc k->k-1 with capacity c_k. Conservation makes the backward flow equal the load of intervals crossing the gap. Apply the R02 local feasibility checks A_i+B_i<=H_i first. Recover gap variables from the dual of the uncapped interval-arc circulation or solve the R03 primal at the certified optimum; finite redundant interval caps can add dual multipliers.
transfer: When converting an interval packing LP to a network, prove the load-flow correspondence at every node, keep the edge orientation as a tested invariant, and distinguish the dual flow witness from the primal schedule.
limits: The proof covers positive R02 interval demands after local feasibility checks, fixed vessel order, one berth and nonnegative linear gap costs. The standard-library prototype checks 144 deterministic small integer cases and one reversed-orientation negative control; it is not a production solver or a complexity benchmark. Related interval-flow and weighted-buffer work is established; exact specialization originality unresolved; no operational data or human specialist review.
author: TOTO
